standard.title: Duration and Time Zones
standard.description: solve problems involving duration, including using 12- and 24-hour time across multiple time zones
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can calculate elapsed time and convert between 12- and 24-hour time. Students understand the concept of time zones informally.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students solve problems involving duration and time zone conversion, including multi-zone itinerary and scheduling problems.

nodes.label: Converting between time zones
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students convert times between time zones using UTC offsets and apply 12- and 24-hour time conventions.
nodes.minimum_width: Convert a given time from one time zone to another using a UTC offset.
nodes.typical_width: Convert between multiple time zones; handle day changes; apply to real contexts (flight arrival times, international calls, Perth vs eastern states).
wider: Investigate why time zones exist and how the International Date Line creates calendar day differences.
Explore daylight saving — how does it affect time zone offsets between Australian states, and why is it not observed uniformly?

response_modes.reason: Time zone problems vary significantly: some cross midnight, some cross the date line, some involve daylight saving. Multiple real-world contexts are needed to develop reliable conversion reasoning.

nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 multi-zone scheduling requires chaining multiple individual time zone conversions — students who cannot reliably handle day changes or offset arithmetic in Node 1 produce cascade errors across the multi-zone itinerary.
success_criteria: Correctly converts a time between two given time zones.
Handles day changes correctly when conversion crosses midnight.
Uses 24-hour time appropriately to avoid AM/PM ambiguity.

nodes.label: Solving multi-zone scheduling and itinerary problems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students solve practical problems involving scheduling across multiple time zones, including travel itineraries and virtual meeting planning.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan a meeting time that works for two people in different time zones; show the time in both zones.
nodes.typical_width: Plan an international travel itinerary across multiple time zones; calculate local arrival and departure times; identify scheduling challenges for a multi-national team.
wider: Plan an international travel itinerary across at least three time zones in Asia; calculate all local times; identify the best transit options.
Investigate the practical challenge of regular virtual meetings for a company with staff in different Australian states and an international office — propose a fair meeting time.

response_modes.reason: Multi-zone scheduling requires coordinating UTC offsets, duration calculation, date change reasoning, and 12/24-hour conversion simultaneously — a genuine integration of all time concepts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: International travel itinerary and multi-national scheduling problems offer advancing students rich multi-step applied reasoning — the complexity of coordinating multiple time zones in a realistic scenario is genuinely challenging within Year 8.
success_criteria: Correctly plans a meeting or itinerary accounting for all time zone offsets.
Communicates the solution clearly showing local times in each zone.
